title: Role of videolaryngoscopy during simulated resuscitation
summary:
The current study investigates the general acceptance and application of video visualization of the larynx  vs. direct visualization of the larynx or larynxtube for airway management in resuscitation simulation. In addition the advantages and disadvantages in terms of overall intubation success, number of intubation / failed attempts and time to intubation are in the foreground.

Background is the increased risk of complications in emergency intubations compared to elective direct laryngoscopy as an challenging technique for emergency doctors with less experiences in intubation.

interventions.name:
Resuscitation team of 3 or 4 persons,
Free choice of different airway management devices: videolaryngoscopy, direct laryngoscopy, supraglottic airway management

Resuscitation team of 3 or 4 persons,
Videolaryngoscopy will be the only available device for airway management

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
voluntary appearance in medical training courses (intensive-care, emergency medicine)
Exclusion criteria:
Disaffirmation of video recording
